purpose: Declare this device's Google AICore support the way its own global firmware does, so Play recognises it and can deliver the functional AICore that hosts Gemini Nano.

provenance.device: nezha_eea_global (Xiaomi 17 Ultra EEA) — the global SKU of this same phone
provenance.extraction: A/B payload manifest parsed; only the product partition operation ranges were fetched (3.01 GB of a 9.58 GB archive), then EROFS-extracted.
provenance.note: Same phone model, global regional SKU. No other device identity is involved.

gate_analysis.measured_before: Play refused com.google.android.aicore on this build: "Your device isn't compatible with this version."
gate_analysis.cause: AICore is gated on a declared system feature. The global firmware ships /product/etc/sysconfig/google_aicore.xml declaring com.google.android.feature.AICORE_QC_SM8850 and com.google.android.feature.AICORE_QC. This build declared neither; it declares 24 other com.google.android.feature.* entries and zero AICore ones.
gate_analysis.significance: AICORE_QC_SM8850 names this exact SoC, so Google does support Gemini Nano on this silicon.
gate_analysis.framework_already_wired: PixelConfigOverlayCommon already points config_defaultOnDeviceIntelligenceService at com.google.android.aicore.

deviations_and_risks: The shipped AiCore.apk is a 21 KB Google-signed OEM stub; the functional application is a Play update. Whether Play serves it once the feature is declared is the device result this set exists to measure.

Three permissions the global privapp file lists do not exist in this build: ACCESS_NPU_MODEL_MANAGER_API, MANAGE_AISEAL_VIRTUAL_MACHINE and ATTRIBUTE_WORK_TO_OTHER_APPS. They are Qualcomm/Xiaomi framework additions; unknown names in a privapp allowlist are ignored, but an AICore path that needs the NPU model manager may not work.
This build reports a Pixel fingerprint (google/mustang_beta/mustang). Declaring a Qualcomm AICore feature alongside it is inconsistent, and Play may key on more than the feature alone.
